title: Bridge streaming embedding responses to cursored pagination: compatibility adapter and error normalization
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: New streaming embeddings and reranker responses (used by improved latency-sensitive clients) differ from legacy cursored pagination + HTTP error contracts. Several partners and older SDKs expect deterministic page cursors, stable item ordering, and specific HTTP error mappings (409/429/500 semantics). This ticket scopes a compatibility adapter that translates streaming outputs into a cursored pagination surface and normalizes runtime errors to the legacy error contract so downstream clients (and self-hosted integrations) do not require code changes. The adapter will also provide opt-in features for structured output preservation (scores, annotations, and tool-call metadata) while ensuring page size/backpressure semantics are respected.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter exposes a paged /v1/embeddings.list style endpoint that consumes streaming model output and returns cursor tokens compatible with existing SDKs
Cursor tokens are stable for the lifetime of a document set and support forward-only traversal; tokens include opaque server-side pointer and checksum to detect staleness

Error mapping layer converts streaming/runtime failures into documented legacy HTTP error codes with consistent error shapes (rate_limit -> 429, transient infra -> 503, idempotency/dup -> 409 where appropriate)
Structured fields (score, annotations, tool metadata) are preserved in page payloads and documented in the adapter contract
End-to-end integration tests with two representative legacy SDKs pass (pagination, next_cursor semantics, retry on transient errors)

ENG: implement error mapping middleware and test harness (ENG-52500)
Add E2E tests with legacy SDKs and CI gating
Add observability: per-cursor latency, buffer occupancy, error-rate by mapped-code, and a migration dashboard
Design: update SDK docs and example migration guide
Rollout plan: staged enablement for existing customers via feature flag, monitor errors for 72h before broad enablement
design_notes: Tradeoffs: buffering streaming tokens to produce pages introduces added memory and change to tail latency; we use bounded per-request window + configurable page-size to control memory and SLO impact
Cursor format: opaque base64 of (backend-pointer, checksum, expiry-timestamp). We will not encode application data in cursor to keep backward compatibility and prevent leakage
Ordering: preserve model emission order; ties are stable by emission timestamp + sequence index to avoid flakiness in sort-dependent clients
Partial pages: adapter will allow returning partial pages with a 'partial': true flag when upstream stalls; legacy clients must be able to continue with returned next_cursor
Deduplication: adapter will dedupe identical embeddings within a small rolling window (configurable), but provide a signal in metadata if deduping occurred
Idempotency: provide request-id echo in cursor metadata to detect retries and avoid duplicate consumption in long-running streams
